lead.headline: Voters rejected data center projects in 40 of 41 US ballot measures
lead.hook: AI data centers were on US ballots 41 times in 10 states on Tuesday, and ==voters sided with them just once==.
points: The questions covered moratoriums, rezonings and advisory votes for local officials, many in Ohio. Six more came earlier this year and three are still to come.
In Wells, Maine, over 80% of voters approved a retroactive 180-day moratorium on data center development.
The lone win was Harwood, North Dakota. Voters rejected, by about three to one, extra review of industrial projects including data centers. A $3 billion data center is already being built nearby.
Democratic governors-elect Gina Hinojosa (Texas), Keisha Lance Bottoms (Georgia) and Amy Acton (Ohio) campaigned on data center regulation.
Texas holds about a quarter of US data center capacity in the works, so __tighter Texas rules could slow the national build-out__.
signal: If local opposition keeps winning at this rate, siting and power approvals become the binding cost of AI capacity, not chips alone.
Separately today, AI data center stocks fell on Wednesday as investors priced in regulation.
lead.editors_read: Local ballots are cheap for voters to use and hard for developers to fight, so expect more of them. The three governors-elect control permitting and utility regulation in big data center states, which makes state rules the next battleground. Companies with signed power and land will gain an edge over those still seeking approvals.

frontpage.headline: Trump's midterm loss may help India in trade talks, but complicates ratification
frontpage.hook: Democrats won Congress, and Indian experts say India's leverage in US trade talks rises even as ratifying a deal gets harder; India's exports to the US were $87 billion last fiscal.
points: The US embassy in New Delhi says Trump remains firmly in charge of trade policy and the midterms don't change its commitment to India.
Any trade deal needs Congress backing to be ratified, which a Democratic Congress could make harder, experts say.
Former WTO ambassador Jayant Dasgupta says it will be difficult for Trump to give India a clear edge over competitors while Congress support is uncertain.
Brent crude fell 8.9% to $94.29, its lowest since 4 September, after Trump played down Iran strikes. The rupee closed at 94.46 per dollar, 29 paise stronger.
Experts flag near-term escalation risk in West Asia before the new Congress convenes in January.
signal: If a weaker White House softens on Russian oil purchases, India gains room to bargain, but only on terms Congress will accept.
Lower crude helps India's import bill and rupee as long as West Asia tensions don't flare.
frontpage.editors_read: The two forces pull against each other: a weaker president concedes more, but a deal he signs is less certain to survive Congress. India probably gains most from slow talks and a lower oil price rather than a quick deal. Goyal wants an export advantage over competitors first, and that is the hardest term to deliver now.

frontpage.headline: Razorpay gets SEBI approval for IPO of about ₹5,000-6,000 crore
frontpage.hook: Razorpay has SEBI approval for an IPO of roughly ₹5,000-6,000 crore at about a $5 billion valuation, with listing likely between January and March 2027, sources say.
points: The IPO is expected to mix fresh shares and an offer-for-sale (existing holders selling); the split is not known. Bankers reported include Axis Capital, Kotak, JP Morgan and Citi.
The valuation is below the $7.5 billion of its 2021 round. It filed confidentially in June.

Razorpay moved its domicile from the US to India, paying about $150 million in taxes, and turned loss-making in FY25 on ₹1,209 crore of ESOP (employee stock) costs and one-time restructuring and tax costs.
Operating revenue rose 65% to ₹3,783 crore in FY25.
Rival PhonePe paused its IPO in March 2026 over West Asia tensions and volatile markets; it had planned to raise over $1 billion.
signal: If Razorpay lists at about $5 billion, it sets a public-market price for Indian payments firms that is well below 2021 private marks.
Its AI push (Vulcan payments model, Agent Studio with about 200 beta businesses) is how it will argue for growth beyond payment processing.
frontpage.editors_read: The IPO happens at a discount to the 2021 peak, so investors who bought then take a markdown. Razorpay going first while PhonePe waits shows who is ready, and a good reception would let PhonePe restart.

frontpage.headline: AI chip startup Agrani Labs nears $108-110 million round at about $350 million valuation
frontpage.hook: Agrani Labs is closing a $108-110 million round at a valuation of around $350 million, led by Peak XV, people aware of the matter told ET.
points: Peak XV Partners is expected to put in more than half of the total.
Google, Samsung Ventures and Stargazer, the investment vehicle linked to Groww's founders, are also expected to participate.
The round has been in the works for several months and is expected to close over the next month.
signal: If it closes, the round is large relative to its valuation, so investors are paying for a chip team's potential rather than revenue.
frontpage.editors_read: Strategic investors like Google and Samsung typically want supply or design access, not just returns. Agrani's valuation is modest next to other AI chip rounds in today's paper, which makes it a cheaper bet on India-based chip design.

frontpage.headline: India approves $1.5 billion subsidy for 92 GWh of energy storage
frontpage.hook: India will spend 145 billion rupees ($1.5 billion) in subsidies to help build 92 gigawatt-hours of energy storage capacity through 2031.
points: Information minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the plan in New Delhi on Wednesday.
The reason: India has been adding more solar and wind capacity than the grid can absorb.
The subsidy is meant to help companies in the nascent storage sector start operations and make better use of renewable plants and transmission lines.
The funding runs through 2031.
signal: If storage gets built on schedule, more solar and wind output can be used instead of curtailed, improving returns on renewable projects.
Battery makers and developers are the direct beneficiaries; the subsidy works out to about $16 per kWh of the target capacity.

frontpage.headline: Indian IT firms race to train forward-deployed engineers
frontpage.hook: 88% of surveyed enterprises expect demand for forward-deployed engineers to rise by 2030, yet only 1% of engineers hold explicit FDE roles, a Scaler-CMR report found.
points: FDEs work directly with customers to find business problems, build AI solutions and take them into production, owning the whole deployment.
HCLTech onboarded 6,136 freshers in the September quarter, about 15% in its elite category, to train as FDEs, and is launching an FDE Academy with OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, Google and Nvidia tracks.
LTM is both hiring FDEs and retraining staff. Scaler's Amar Srivastava says the long-term plan is 60-70% in-house talent.
Wipro's AI-native unit has over 2,000 engineers including FDEs. Coforge is moving to hybrid teams of engineers and AI agents.
signal: The role needs technical, business and client skills at once, which classroom training can't supply, so experienced hybrid profiles will stay scarce and well paid.
For a business generalist, the client-facing, outcome-owning part of this role is where non-engineers can compete.

frontpage.headline: Agility Robotics goes public via SPAC at $2.5 billion valuation
frontpage.hook: Agility Robotics, expected to start trading on Nasdaq Thursday as the first US-listed humanoid company, made just $1.8 million revenue last year against a $138.1 million net loss.
points: It merged with Churchill Capital Corp XI, a SPAC (shell company that lists a business by merger), at an equity value of about $2.5 billion, expecting about $465 million gross capital.
More than half of revenue came from five robots bought by one investor. It used $99.8 million cash in 2025 and lost $2.7 million on sales alone.
Its Digit robot works in nine customer facilities including Amazon, Toyota and GXO. A filing cites over $300 million in orders for 1,000 robots from one customer, contingent on meeting deadlines.
Private rivals are valued higher: Figure AI about $39 billion, Neura about $7 billion, Apptronik about $5.5 billion.
Chinese firms made about 90% of humanoid shipments last year; the FCC banned new foreign-made advanced robots in July.
signal: If Agility's stock holds, it becomes the public benchmark for humanoid valuations; a slump would pressure much richer private marks.
Deliveries are targeted for the first half of 2027, so unit economics are unproven until then.
frontpage.editors_read: The market is pricing a shipping-but-unprofitable company far below pre-revenue rivals. That gap will close either by Agility rising on execution or the private valuations falling. The single-customer order is both its biggest asset and its biggest risk.

frontpage.headline: India approves $297 million incentives for lithium and nickel processing
frontpage.hook: India's cabinet approved ₹28.14 billion ($297 million) in incentives to boost domestic processing of lithium and nickel, reducing reliance on China-dominated supply chains.
points: The programme supports turning lithium and nickel ores and intermediates into high-purity compounds.
Named beneficiaries: electric mobility, battery energy storage, electronics, defence and speciality steel.
The government cites China's export controls and heavy import dependence on critical minerals as supply-chain risks.
signal: Battery storage and EV makers get a nearer, more secure input source if domestic refining actually scales.
Separately today, India approved a ₹14,500 crore battery storage subsidy, so demand and materials policies now point in the same direction.

frontpage.headline: AI inference startup Fal raises $1.3 billion at $16 billion valuation
frontpage.hook: Fal doubled its valuation to $16 billion with a $1.3 billion round led by Bessemer in October, six months after an $8 billion valuation.
points: Fal hosts image, video and audio models for creators and developers, and runs them after training (inference).
Nvidia, Sound Ventures, HOF Capital and T. Rowe Price also invested. The previous round was $350 million, led by Sequoia, in April.
CEO Burkay Gur says the raise was partly to buy computing power: in summer Fal 'was not able to serve customers and had to rate limit them'.
Modal and Baseten are also reported to be in talks to raise at steep valuations.
signal: Demand for running models is outrunning supply of computing power, so inference firms are raising money mainly to buy capacity.
Separately, data center opposition on US ballots could tighten that capacity further.
frontpage.editors_read: Fal's growth shows inference demand, but a business that must raise this much to buy compute has costs that scale with usage. Watch whether margins hold as capacity grows.

stories.headline: Democratic win splits tech stocks: hyperscalers up, AI chip and data centre names down
stories.hook: After Democrats took Congress, Amazon rose 8%, Microsoft and Apple 6% each, adding over $750 billion in combined value, while CoreWeave fell 11%.
points: Alphabet gained 5.7% and Meta 3.5%. Apple jumped nearly 7% to a record high.
Losers: SanDisk -10%, Seagate down as much as 8.2%, Nvidia -2.5%, AMD -1.5% despite strong earnings.
Some investors think tighter AI and data centre rules may make hyperscalers moderate spending, which would help their cash flow.
Big Tech plans over $740 billion in spending this year versus about $400 billion last year, turning cash-rich firms into borrowers.
signal: Markets read less AI capex as good for spenders and bad for suppliers.
Democratic wins in Ohio, Georgia and Texas matter because those states have large planned data centre investments.

stories.headline: India nears release of AI regulation consultation paper
stories.hook: India's AI regulation consultation paper is close to final, with public feedback expected soon, after minister Ashwini Vaishnaw first promised it within a month on October 8.
points: It is expected to cover AI safety, deepfakes, psychological effects on users, skilling and wider access to AI's gains.
Vaishnaw said on October 23 that responses would be sought from citizens, businesses and AI users, and that legislation may be warranted.
It builds on the India AI Governance Guidelines of November 2025, which set seven principles including human oversight and accountability proportionate to harm.
The guidelines proposed an AI Governance Group, an expert committee and an AI Safety Institute.
signal: If legislation follows, accountability for AI harm, training-data copyright and data protection are the likely gaps to be filled.

stories.headline: Isomorphic Labs in talks to raise about $5 billion at up to $50 billion valuation
stories.hook: Alphabet's Isomorphic Labs is in talks to raise roughly $5 billion at a valuation of about $50 billion, five months after a $2.1 billion Series B.
points: The AI drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind; the deal has not closed and terms could change.
It was founded in 2021 on AlphaFold, DeepMind's protein structure prediction system.
It has partnerships with Eli Lilly and Novartis and develops its own medicines in cancer and immune disorders.
No AI-designed medicine has yet reached the market, and few AI drug firms have reached clinical trials.
signal: The valuation prices in success before any clinical proof; the test is trial results, which take years.

stories.headline: Three-month-old chip startup Tenspresso in talks at $500 million valuation
stories.hook: Tenspresso, founded three months ago by former Google AI chip engineers, is in talks for financing that would value it at $500 million.
points: Weeks after raising $20 million from Striker Venture Partners, Altimeter Capital approached it about an additional investment.
The company made a few key hires after its first round.
signal: Investors are paying for team pedigree before any product, as in Agrani Labs' round today.

also.line: OpenAI is acquiring Pierre Computer, whose Trees and Diffs libraries already power Codex's code review, to build Git tooling for coding agents; open-source projects stay open and closing needs regulatory approval.
Figma banking on AI credits, in-house model to lift margins (source unreachable — headline only)

stories.headline: Peppermint Robotics raises ₹100 crore for cleaning robots
stories.hook: Pune-based Peppermint Robotics raised ₹100 crore (about $10.5 million) in a pre-Series B led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners, with revenue up nearly sixfold from FY24 to FY26.
points: Asiana Fund also joined; the round mixes new capital and secondary share sales. It last raised ₹34 crore in April 2025 and has raised ₹150 crore in total.
Its robots scrub floors and move materials in factories, hospitals, airports and warehouses, selling mainly to facility management companies.
It operates in nine countries; the US is the biggest market. Its cleanroom robots passed qualification in an EU GMP Grade cleanroom.
Funds go to manufacturing capacity, next-generation robots, hiring and a planned North American assembly line.
signal: Revenue doubled last year and is growing from a small base; the US assembly line shows where its demand sits.

stories.headline: EloElo raises $80 million for micro drama platform Story TV
stories.hook: EloElo Group raised $80 million in a Series C led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal, taking total funding to $130 million.
points: Story TV has over 5,000 micro dramas in six languages and users spend 95 minutes a day, the company says; its apps have over 40 million monthly users.
Sources say annualised collections rose more than tenfold to about $250 million in a year.
EloElo reported FY25 revenue of ₹69.5 crore with losses largely flat, and says it has profitable unit economics.
Money goes to original content, a US launch of Story TV and its Dolphin AI creative suite.
Rivals include Kuku TV, ShareChat's Quick TV and Flipkart; Omdia expects the global micro drama industry to earn $14 billion by end-2026.
signal: A US launch will test whether Indian micro drama economics travel; NBCUniversal's backing helps with content distribution.

also.line: India now has 51 startups valued above $500 million, worth about ₹3.3 lakh crore ($34.1 billion) combined, averaging about ₹6,400 crore each and employing over 60,000 people, with few AI entities.

stories.headline: L&T explores manufacturing bets from tunnel boring machines to rockets
stories.hook: L&T is exploring at least half a dozen new manufacturing businesses to cut reliance on projects, as manufacturing is only 6% of its ₹1.47 trillion first-half FY27 revenue.
points: Options include nuclear fuel rods, tunnel boring machines, rockets, drones, BESS, EV traction motors and prefabricated housing units; they are at different stages and may not all proceed.
L&T wants to at least double manufacturing's contribution; it already makes howitzers, rocket launchers, warships and valves.
Analyst Amit Anwani says manufacturing margins can exceed 15% versus 8-9% for infrastructure, but need more R&D and capacity investment.
The company nears ₹3 trillion in annual revenue and seeks 12-15% growth. Finance and tech make up 29% of revenue.
signal: Several bets depend on policy opening, such as private nuclear and space sectors; if those open, L&T's order book moves toward higher-margin products.

also.line: IIT Gandhinagar startup Cellegant Energy Systems raised ₹2.61 crore from GVFL and others to build hydrogen-powered drones, aiming to demonstrate a 35-kg model with longer endurance.

stories.headline: Tests suggest AI models can detect tampering with their internals, not describe it
stories.hook: In Anthropic's 2025 experiment, the newest Claude models correctly flagged an injected 'thought' in 20% of trials, and control copies never falsely reported one.
points: Researcher Jack Lindsey boosted neural patterns for a concept like denim in half the model copies, then asked if they detected an injected thought.
Follow-ups by Lederman and Mahowald split the question in two: detecting an injection and naming it. Naming looks like steering alone, since models often said 'apple' when wrong.
Detection resisted their controls, so they call it 'anomaly detection', something never trained for.
Whether that counts as introspection is disputed; smaller-model researchers are still testing simpler explanations.
signal: If anomaly detection is reliable, it could become a tool for spotting tampering with models, though 20% is far from reliable.

also.line: India drew nearly $400 billion of investment interest at its renewable summit, almost double the $220 billion needed by 2030; minister Pralhad Joshi says 300 GW more non-fossil capacity is planned for 2030-2036 beyond the 500 GW target.

Google is offering voluntary exit packages in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland to curb costs amid AI spending, despite headcount rising to 204,757; the payout is up to 12 months' salary.

stories.headline: Democrats won Congress but face limits on Trump's tariffs, Iran war and immigration
stories.hook: Democrats won both chambers, but take control only in January and Trump says 'I'll veto everything', so their main tools are investigations and spending.
points: Most Senate bills need 60 votes, and Trump can veto; overriding needs a two-thirds majority.
Committees can subpoena and investigate, including Trump family wealth, which has risen about $2.2 billion since his term began per disclosures.
Experts say blocking new war funding is their strongest limit on the Iran war; the party has historically avoided cutting military funds.
On immigration, some want to claw back about $240 billion given for enforcement; a poll found 65% say ICE has gone too far.
Impeachment would need two-thirds of the Senate to remove anyone.
signal: Attaching health and spending measures to must-pass budget bills is the likeliest route to results; trade relief is less so.

also.line: The UK government is considering restricting smart glasses, possibly banning sales to certain users, over concerns they are used to secretly film women, safeguarding minister Satvir Kaur told the Commons.

stories.headline: Weak monsoon forces India to put food before ethanol
stories.hook: India's ethanol blend in petrol may fall to 15-17% this supply year from the 20% target, after the weakest monsoon in over a decade cut rainfall about 13%.
points: Corn and sugar prices rose about 40% to records, rice 20%, and retail food inflation hit 7.74% in September from 5.97% in August.
The government told oil companies not to buy sugar-based ethanol this season and cut corn-based ethanol's price to ₹68.86 a litre from ₹71.86.
Corn output may fall up to 15% from a record 55 million tonnes; rice stocks are an option but costly, since the state sells grain to distillers at about half its cost.
Producers built about 20 billion litres of annual capacity and now face overcapacity.
E20 has saved nearly ₹2 lakh crore in oil imports since 2014, about ₹43,000 crore a year.
signal: Lower blending raises crude import needs, and food inflation matters politically before 2027 state elections including Uttar Pradesh.

stories.headline: India faces prolonged food inflation across grains, chicken and milk
stories.hook: Food inflation could reach around 10% in the December quarter, as the weakest monsoon in a decade, costly feed and a weaker rupee lift grain, poultry and dairy prices.
points: A farmer in the report wants to plant wheat and chickpeas for good prices but lacks water after below-average rains.
signal: Costly feed passes through to poultry and dairy, so price pressure spreads beyond grains.

also.line: The Cotton Association of India expects 2026-27 output to fall about 14% to 280 lakh bales from 325.69 lakh as drought hits Maharashtra; closing stocks fall to 40.88 lakh bales.

stories.headline: Mounjaro becomes India's top-selling drug as GLP-1 market nears ₹3,000 crore
stories.hook: Eli Lilly's Mounjaro sold about ₹1,736 crore in the year to September 2026, making it India's top-selling drug, in a GLP-1 market of ₹2,596 crore.
points: It launched in March 2025 and sold ₹923 crore in 2025-26. Injectables are about 86% of the GLP-1 market.
Generic semaglutide arrived after Novo Nordisk's patent expired in March 2026; monthly sales rose from ₹48 crore to ₹113 crore by September and units rose sixteen-fold, 74% generic.
Monthly treatment costs ₹1,850-8,000 for semaglutide. India has 254 million people with obesity and 101 million with diabetes, per an ICMR-INDIAB study.
A diabetologist says there are 50 brands and 8-9 device types, and keeping patients on therapy for a year is the first hurdle.
Multinationals now launch patented drugs in India 2-3 years after global launch, down from 7-8, per OPPI.
signal: If patients pay for brand and delivery experience, Indian generic firms must compete on retention and support, not price alone.

stories.headline: Meta lawsuit claims AI tools shaped layoffs; workers fear algorithmic firing
stories.hook: 26 anonymous former Meta employees sued in July, alleging AI-enabled systems helped pick who was laid off and hit people on disability or parental leave hardest.
points: Plaintiffs say AI-adoption dashboards did not account for protected leave. Meta denies it: 'AI did not select anyone for termination.'
A Fast Company LinkedIn poll of over 480 people found over two-thirds worried about AI choosing layoffs; 37% were 'very' concerned.
Experts say direct AI layoff lists are limited, but employers use work intelligence tools to judge which jobs AI could replace.
A few states already require transparency on AI in termination decisions; Workday and Eightfold face lawsuits over hiring.
signal: If courts accept leave-blind metrics as discrimination, companies using such dashboards face legal risk.

stories.headline: Neurotech wearables are training AI brain models on user data, often without clear consent
stories.hook: Interaxon, maker of the Muse headband, has trained a brain AI model on about 50,000 hours of EEG data from users who were not explicitly asked.
points: A Science investigation reviewed dozens of privacy policies and found tens of millions of hours of consumer EEG data collected, largely unregulated.
Nine neurotech and AI software firms have publicly acknowledged building a brain foundation model.
Once data is embedded in a model, it is near-impossible to remove.
Of the privacy policies reviewed, all but one allow sharing with third parties in anonymized or aggregated forms, and all either permit or do not rule out sharing with authorities.
Consumer headsets have 1-6 electrodes versus 19-25 clinical; experts doubt an all-purpose brain model is feasible on such data.
signal: Expect pressure for neural-data consent rules; UNESCO and the OECD have flagged consumer brain devices.

stories.headline: AI agents run a self-driving DNA lab in Shanghai
stories.hook: Shanghai Jiao Tong University's AutoDNA lab uses AI agents to design and run DNA experiments across more than 20 instrument types from a simple human prompt.
points: Robot arms move samples; humans only refresh reagents and service hardware.
It was built around AI from the start, whereas most systems add AI to one step and still need experts to configure instruments.
Tests included detecting a cancer-linked mutation and encoding a quote in DNA.
signal: Self-driving labs could cut the human hands-on time per experiment, shifting scientist work to question design.

opportunities.name: SLAY HACKS 2026
opportunities.summary: Month-long online AI hackathon on Devpost with $5,000 in prizes ($2,000 grand prize, $500 best beginner). Open to students, developers and builders worldwide; online/global.

opportunities.name: EDSAFE AI Fellowship 2027
opportunities.when: Apply by Mon 30 Nov, 10 p.m. EST
opportunities.summary: Part-time leadership fellowship on safe and equitable AI in education, with workshops, mentorship and a capstone project. Fellows announced in January 2027; online/global.
